ana: Quick scorecard from the atlas11b bring-up (int6 vs int8). TL;DR: int6 for latency-sensitive chat, int8 for high-throughput background workloads. Short summary below.

mike: Nice — can you drop the key numbers?

ana: Sure. High-level bullets: 
- atlas11b-int6 (FP16-ish/perf-tuned): p50 ~95ms, p95 ~210ms, unit tokens/$1k ≈ 1.8M, quality delta vs baseline (13b fp16) ~ -0.2% overall, no major regressions on long-form.
- atlas11b-int8 (post-quant): p50 ~110ms, p95 ~700ms, unit tokens/$1k ≈ 5.6M (+3.1x), quality delta ~ -0.8% (helpfulness), regression concentrated on multi-turn long-context where hallucination score rises slightly.
- Tail story: int8 shows intermittent p99 spikes on long sequences (KV cache pressure + kernel fallback). Seen at ~1 in 10k requests in our synthetic chat QA slice.

sophie: Can you quantify the quality hits? ROUGE/EM or our internal helpfulness?

ana: Internal helpfulness drop: -0.6% absolute (statistically significant on n=12k eval queries, p<0.01). ROUGE-L on long summaries: -0.9 relative. Short prompt QA: ~ -0.1. So short-chat mostly fine.

eval-bot: eval-bot: automated snapshot attached -> 
```
model: atlas11b-int8
slice: multi-turn-long
tokens: 12,456
helpfulness_delta: -0.006
rouge_l_delta: -0.009
p50_latency_ms: 110
p95_latency_ms: 700
notes: p99 spikes correlated with seq_len>2048
```

tj: Oof: p95 700ms is concerning for customer-facing chat if it occasionally pops up. Is that reproducible on dedicated pools?

ana: Reproducible in hosted env at high concurrency (burst>200 rps per GPU), but in Dedicated private pools with slightly larger KV cache allocation the p95 drops ~20%. We saw two clear mitigations: increase kv_cache_capacity, or route seq_len>1024 to int6 fallback.

ana: Proposed routing + config (quick):
```
quant:
  mode: int8
  per_channel: true
routing:
  p50_target_ms: 120
  fallback: atlas11b-int6
  seq_len_threshold: 1024
batching:
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  dynamic_batch_timeout_ms: 6
```

mike: Solid. Recommendation for GTN/product? What's the suggested default route and pricing signal?

ana: My recs: 
- Default for new chat endpoints: atlas11b-int6. Keeps latency & quality predictable.
- Background/async tasks (rerank, embeddings proxy, batch summarize): atlas11b-int8 to save ~3x on token cost.
- Add canary flag to test int8 on 10% of non-critical traffic with automatic rollback if helpfulness delta < -0.5% or p95 > 400ms.

sophie: I'll own the canary A/B eval. Suggest 48h run with these metrics: helpfulness, rouge_l, p95 latency, p99 error spikes, and tokens/$1k.

tj: Make sure ops has autoscale tuned — int8 bursts are cheaper but amplify kv-cache pressure. Also add a jittered retry on our client side for p99s.

ana: Created ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-4571 (adds scorecard row, routing flags, canary plan). I'll also add the per-slice signal thresholds to the scorecard.

mike: Thanks. Once sophie posts the 24h interim, we'll present to GTN & product to update recommended routing and default pricing tier suggestions. :thumbsup:

sophie: Will run today, expect first 24h report tomorrow morning.

ana: Summary action items: [ana] add scorecard + thresholds, [sophie] run 48h A/B, [tj] ops tuning, [mike] GTN sync after 24h.

mike: 👍
